searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he remaining work — geelooy revival audit the awtsmoos renews the screen each instant; the vessel must become lucid, useful, and bright. awtsmoos.com should reveal one clear next action, not bury living function beneath decorative night. mission audit the public routes represented by geelooy, use the existing route/runtime quality machinery instead of rebuilding it, repair broken or cluttered surfaces only after real source/runtime tracing, and avoid overwriting concurrent agent work. direct evidence geelooy is the public/static source root; browser urls omit the geelooy path segment. earlier census found 228 html/page documents and already created modular cdp runtime audit tooling under scripts/runtime quality/. current worktree is heavily dirty with multiple concurrent agents. shema strike, ohrfront, social composer, animator, mitzvah world, and runtime audit tooling have active modifications. geelooy/mawgawl is currently clean and is therefore the safest screenshot owned surface for immediate reconstruction. sefarim currently presents hero, guarantees, multi mode controls, scope tabs, results, indexed lanes, history, and guidance simultaneously. user screenshots also show poor game affordance/visual hierarchy, a mostly blank animator canvas, and a crowded social composer. concurrency guard [ ] never reset, clean, stash, checkout, or discard unrelated work. [ ] re check scoped git status immediately before each production write. [ ] treat directories with active agent edits as audit only until ownership becomes safe. [ ] prefer clean route families for first implementation waves. discovery work [ ] read all sefarim html/css/js owners that determine visible hierarchy. [ ] trace sefarim search modes, progressive disclosure, history, and result rendering. [ ] run existing runtime audit against /mawgawl/sefarim/ before mutation. [ ] capture dom metrics at desktop and mobile widths. [ ] build representative route matrix across core, torah, social, apps, games, editors, media, auth, docs, and os surfaces. [ ] run a bounded whole surface crawl after the first safe route is repaired. [ ] classify each finding as runtime failure, layout failure, interaction failure, accessibility failure, visual hierarchy debt, or intentional behavior. sefarim reconstruction work [ ] make search the unmistakable primary action. [ ] collapse secondary search modes into progressive disclosure rather than permanent first viewport weight. [ ] reduce simultaneous side rail competition. [ ] keep results immediately adjacent to the query task. [ ] preserve provenance, exact coordinates, persisted index truth, and existing query parameters. [ ] preserve keyboard, screen reader, history, and api behavior. [ ] make mobile layout one column and touch safe without horizontal overflow. [ ] ensure empty, loading, error, and populated states each have a clear visual hierarchy. [ ] keep every touched source file <=120 lines; split before rewriting a larger responsibility. [ ] rewrite touched files completely with tabs where indentation exists. wider public surface work [ ] audit shema strike runtime and gameplay ergonomics without overwriting its active edits. [ ] audit ohrfront runtime/gameplay clarity without overwriting its active edits. [ ] audit animator blank canvas/root layout failure without overwriting its active edits. [ ] audit social composer hierarchy after the active redesign agent finishes or ownership clears. [ ] audit game index discoverability and every game entry route for load/runtime failures. [ ] audit partially styled/native controls, viewport overflow, fixed/sticky collisions, and missing interaction states identified by the prior sitewide ledger. verification work [ ] read back every touched file in full. [ ] run syntax/source architecture tests for touched js modules. [ ] run focused sefarim tests and add missing regression contracts only after implementation. [ ] browser test query submission and each search mode. [ ] browser test 430px mobile, standard desktop, and short height viewport. [ ] confirm no site owned console errors, failed static resources, mime mismatches, or accidental overflow. [ ] compare planned versus actual changes and write delta artifacts. [ ] repeat implementation if any delta remains. next action write the three mandatory planning waves grounded in this evidence, then inspect the remaining sefarim owners and run the existing runtime gate before any production rewrite.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase one — boundless geelooy revival brainstorm the awtsmoos makes each pixel possible anew; awtsmoos.com can therefore reveal simplicity without becoming plain. the ideal is not fewer capabilities, but capabilities arranged so intention arrives before ornament and function before strain. north star imagine every public surface behaving like one coherent civilization: a user knows where they are, what matters now, what action comes next, what succeeded, and how to recover when it fails. unlimited possibilities 1. a global route health map that discovers every public entry and records runtime, layout, interaction, accessibility, and performance signals. 2. a public quality dashboard that groups pages by healthy, degraded, broken, blocked by auth, and intentional tooling status. 3. a shared shell vocabulary for headers, back navigation, page title, primary action, contextual rail, status, empty state, and mobile drawer. 4. a universal progressive disclosure contract: advanced controls stay available but do not compete with the primary task. 5. a density budget per viewport so pages cannot silently accumulate five simultaneous panels. 6. a visual hierarchy budget that limits equal weight headings, borders, glows, pills, and competing accent colors. 7. a responsive contract that guarantees one column task flow at phone width unless the task genuinely requires a canvas. 8. a game acceptance harness that verifies start, movement/input, objective progress, restart/recovery, hud legibility, and win/fail transitions. 9. a canvas/app acceptance harness that distinguishes an intentionally blank work area from a failed render. 10. a browser journey library that can exercise search, social publishing, editors, games, media, login, and navigation with reusable primitives. 11. route screenshots at canonical desktop, phone, and short height sizes for human comparison. 12. dom measurements for overflow, touch targets, unnamed controls, hidden focus, excessive fixed layers, and empty canvases. 13. performance budgets for route load, long tasks, animation pressure, and oversized asset waterfalls. 14. shared motion tokens that disable ornamental movement under reduced motion without breaking feedback. 15. shared spacing/type tokens that reduce the tendency for every feature to invent a new visual language. 16. page local css ownership so a repair does not destabilize unrelated routes. 17. explicit state styling for loading, error, empty, success, disabled, selected, active, hover, focus visible, and offline states. 18. game specific onboarding overlays that teach controls only until the player demonstrates competence. 19. game huds that hide secondary metrics until context makes them useful. 20. editor workspaces that reserve the largest visual region for content rather than tool chrome. 21. search surfaces that foreground query + results and move libraries/history/help into optional context. 22. social creation that uses a guided progression instead of displaying every destination and content type at once. 23. a route registry generated from real files but curated with semantics: public, dynamic, fixture, template, legacy, internal tool, and experimental. 24. a route debt ledger linking every broken symptom to owning files, test evidence, and completion proof. 25. a concurrency aware repair scheduler that avoids routes currently owned by active agents. 26. a shared “clear task” design review rule: one primary action, one obvious status, one dominant content region. 27. automated checks that prohibit accidental horizontal overflow and unreachable fixed controls. 28. a game input abstraction that tests keyboard, pointer, and touch paths where each game claims support. 29. a public index audit so working apps/games are discoverable and dead ones are not promoted as finished. 30. a graceful experimental badge/status model for unfinished experiences instead of pretending every prototype is production ready. five competing architectures a — global redesign layer apply one universal stylesheet and shell across every route. fast visual convergence, but dangerously invasive and likely to create cascade regressions. b — route by route reconstruction repair each route locally with strict ownership. safest behaviorally, but risks visual drift and duplicated solutions. c — shared contracts + local skins define small cross site contracts for hierarchy, responsiveness, states, and accessibility while keeping route local css/components. strong balance of coherence and containment. d — runtime gate first build quality tooling and change only routes that fail measurable gates. excellent evidence discipline, but subjective clutter can survive if metrics are too narrow. e — journey first product repair select representative user journeys, repair them end to end, then expand by category. strong user value, but route coverage can lag. preferred synthesis use c + d + e: shared quality contracts, measured runtime gates, and end to end journey reconstruction. avoid a giant global visual override. the awtsmoos can be one without making every vessel identical; coherence should come from principles, not one monolithic stylesheet. first safe journey /mawgawl/sefarim/ is the first implementation candidate because its source tree is clean while screenshot adjacent game/social/app surfaces are under active modification. next action map theoretical files and responsibilities for the sefarim reconstruction plus the sitewide audit path, then critique this phase before any production code is changed.
